title: Why Do We Get Hiccups? 😲 Fun Facts for Kids
description:
Hiccups start with a muscle under your lungs! Leo asks, big sister Mia explains what makes the 'hic' sound, in under a minute.

Curio Kids Club: short, curious answers to kids' big questions. Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@CurioKidsClub

lines.text: Mia, why do we get hiccups? Hic!
It starts with a muscle under your lungs called the diaphragm. It helps you breathe in and out.
Usually it moves smoothly, down and up. But sometimes it gives a sudden little jump!
And that makes the hic sound?
Yes! The jump makes you suck in air fast. Then your vocal cords in your throat snap shut. Hic!
Often it's eating too fast, gulping fizzy drinks, or laughing a lot. A very full tummy can bother it too.
But why do we have hiccups at all?
That's a mystery! Scientists still aren't sure. Even babies hiccup, before they're born!
How do I make them stop?
Good news: hiccups usually stop on their own after a few minutes. Some people find that slow, calm breaths help.
A jumpy diaphragm, a gulp of air, and the vocal cords go hic!
Hic! Ha! Follow Curio Kids Club for more wonders. And next time someone asks... why do we get hiccups?
